teaser.en: Too bitter and sour to eat fresh, the Seville orange earns its place in the kitchen and in home medicine.

summary.en: *Mdandzi* is the sour or Seville orange, a citrus tree with bitter-sour fruit grown around homesteads. Its juice is used in cooking and in medicine.

about.en:
*Mdandzi* is an evergreen citrus tree with glossy leaves on winged leaf stalks, often thorny, with very fragrant white flowers.

The fruit looks like an orange, with a rough, thick skin, but its pulp is sour and bitter rather than sweet.

where.en: *Mdandzi* is a homestead tree, grown near houses where its fruit is on hand.

uses.en: The juice is used in cooking, to add a sharp, sour flavour to food. It is also used in medicine.

names.en: Digo: *mdandzi*. Swahili: *mdanzi*. English: sour orange or Seville orange. Scientists call it *Citrus aurantium*.

reason.en: Lime, also used in cooking and medicine

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
